resolvedQuestions: The plugin-owned settings, commands, structured layout, directive writers, and subprocess boundaries are verified from the 2.3.1 source tree.
The requested Beancount directive forms, chronology, balancing weights, assertions, padding, price/include behavior, and lot matching are verified from official documentation.
The BQL execution boundary, current grammar/source tables, dashboard query families, and bean-price output path are verified from plugin and upstream source.
The dashboard/UI feature surface, structured routing, settings effects, and supported versus direct-write workflows are verified from the 2.3.1 source tree.
The layered error catalog, v3 bean-check boundary, CSV/reconciliation workflow, and AI operating recipes are verified or explicitly marked as inference.
keyFindings: data.json is a settings object merged over DEFAULT_SETTINGS; connection readiness is runtime-only.
The generated ledger includes directive files in a fixed order and routes transactions by year or month.
BQL uses parameterized bean-query arguments; price fetching uses bean-price with plugin-side filtering and deduplication.
Writer success is not ledger validation; bean-check remains a required post-write gate.
Posting weights and cost-lot selection, not visual units alone, determine transaction validity.
Dashboard values are typed inventory transformations; row grain, currency selection, and date bounds must be explicit.
bean-price stdout is filtered and appended by the plugin; the plugin does not request in-place update mode.
Dashboard controllers are projections over included Beancount text; the file graph remains the source of truth.
A safe file mutation needs a backup, include check, bean-check, and a small BQL readback.
False-zero results require raw command capture, include verification, currency inspection, and raw inventory readback.
Bulk CSV import is an AI file workflow, not a first-class plugin importer; raw input and running-balance reconciliation are mandatory.
ruledOutDirections: No separate beanquery executable setting key was found.
No supported pad-creation UI was found.
The repository-root compiled main.js was not available at the inspected source ref.
Operating currency does not change ledger processing; balance does not assert total cost basis; pad cannot initialize cost lots.
There is no private database-backed BQL path separate from the configured Beancount executable.
The modal is not a complete editor for pads, bulk imports, or arbitrary metadata.
The plugin has no verified v2.3.1 bean-check service wrapper separate from README capability and editor .errors integration.
observedIdeas: Use data.json only for plugin configuration and vault text as the source of truth for ledger state.
Use filename/lineno BQL readback before any targeted update or delete.
Read open accounts, current balances, and inventory lots before writing.
For every query, state the row grain and valuation basis before trusting a scalar result.
For prices, inspect commodity source metadata, generated output, inclusion, and price date together.
Treat UI-supported writes and direct-file workflows as separate capabilities, then apply the same validation gate.
Classify failures by layer before changing text: parse, lifecycle, weights, assertion/pad, lot, include, BQL/process, price, mutation, or CSV.
